name: Temple of Literature
summary: Walk through the Khue Van gate into the courtyards of Hanoi's Confucian temple, founded in 1070, and the university that followed in 1076. Gates, old trees, and a square pond lead you from one courtyard to the next. Come in the morning before the courtyards fill, or on an evening programme night.
heroCaption: The Khue Van gate at the Temple of Literature
gettingThere: Metro Line 3 stops at Van Mieu station. Walk from there to the gate at 58 Quoc Tu Giam. From Hoan Kiem, take a car or motorbike west.

hours: Operator: 8:00–17:00 daily; evening programme 18:00–22:00 Wed, Sat, Sun. Vietnam Tourism: Tue–Sun, 8:00–17:00 Nov–Mar and 7:30–18:00 the rest of the year; night visit 18:30–21:30.
closed: Operator: open every day. Vietnam Tourism: daytime visits Tuesday–Sunday.
admissionNote: Daytime 70,000 VND (operator and Vietnam Tourism). Priority ticket 35,000 VND; under 16 free (operator). Night ticket: no operator price; Vietnam Tourism lists a 199,000 VND night tour.

notice.title: The night ticket is separate
notice.body: The evening programme on Wednesday, Saturday, and Sunday has its own ticket, apart from the 70,000 VND daytime entry.

body: Enter at 58 Quoc Tu Giam and walk north through the gates. The Khue Van pavilion marks the way into the inner courtyards, and the third courtyard opens around a square pond under old trees. The temple dates to 1070, under Ly Thanh Tong, and the university to 1076.
Go in the morning, before the courtyards fill. On Wednesday, Saturday, and Sunday evenings the temple runs a night programme with its own ticket. Metro Line 3 stops at Van Mieu station.
The Vietnam National Fine Arts Museum, at 66 Nguyen Thai Hoc, is a short walk away if you want a second stop.

figures.caption: The third courtyard and its square pond, under old trees
